sentences.text: Food Inspector vs Shanigaram Satish on 3 July, 2023

The Honourable Sri Justice K.Surender
 Criminal Appeal No.525 Of 2023
Judgment:
1. The Food Inspector filed a complaint against accused on the ground that the packaged drinking water which was sold was not in conformity with the standards.

2 Learned Principal Judicial First Class Magistrate, Warangal found that there is a violation under Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short 'the Act'), since the Food Inspector failed to serve notice informing about the right to get the sample tested.
Admittedly, Food Inspector has not served any notice as required under Section 13(2) of the Act.
3. I do not find any infirmity with the order of the learned Magistrate in acquitting the accused when the mandatory provision under Section 13(2) of the Act is violated.

4. In Ravi Sharma v. State (Government of NCT of Delhi) and another1, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that while dealing with an appeal against acquittal, the appellate court has to consider (2022) 8 Supreme Court Cases 536 whether the trial Court's view can be termed as a possible one,
particularly when evidence on record has been analysed.

entities.text: Ravi Sharma v. State (Government of NCT of Delhi) and another1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The reason is that an order of acquittal adds up to the presumption of innocence in favour of the accused.
Thus, the appellate court has to be relatively slow in reversing the order of the trial court rendering acquittal.

5. In Ghurey Lal v. State of Uttar Pradesh2 the Hon'ble Supreme Court after referring to several Judgments regarding the settled principles of law and the powers of appellate Court in reversing the order of acquittal, held at para 70, as follows:
"70.

entities.text: Ghurey Lal v. State of Uttar Pradesh2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the light of the above, the High Court and other appellate Courts should follow the well-settled principles crystallized by number of Judgments if it is going to overrule or otherwise disturb the trial court's acquittal:
1. The appellate court may only overrule or otherwise disturb the trial court's acquittal if it has "very substantial and compelling reasons"
for doing so.
A number of instances arise in which the appellate court would have "very substantial and compelling reasons" to discard the trial court's decision.

sentences.text: 2. The appellate court must always give proper weight and consideration o the findings of the trial court.

3. If two reasonable views can be reached__ one that leads to acquittal, the other to conviction __the High Courts/appellate courts must rule in favour of the accused."
6.
Accordingly, the Criminal Appeal is dismissed.

Consequently, miscellaneous applications, if any,
shall stand closed.
